summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update5.json → valid=true). New A1 (progress) direction, source-only since this run's experiment capacity is exhausted. installSnapshot's success path updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations, then removes/compacts logs (raft.go:1930-1952) but never calls setLastLog — while the sibling path restoreUserSnapshot explicitly does, with a comment stating the intent (raft.go:1180-1187). Because getLastIndex/getLastEntry return the cached log position whenever it is >= the snapshot position (state.go:152-174), a follower whose cached last index is above the installed snapshot keeps advertising that higher index in every response (raft.go:1443-1449) and takes its prev-log term from its own divergent log instead of the snapshot metadata (raft.go:1475-1502). Where the divergence that triggered the snapshot lies at or below the snapshot index and the leader's log is compacted there, the pair settles into a stable two-state cycle: AppendEntries(PrevLogEntry = snapshotIndex) is rejected with NoRetryBackoff and LastLog = the stale higher index; the back-off clamp only offers min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1) so nextIndex falls to the snapshot index (replication.go:249-261); the request for snapshotIndex-1 cannot be built from the leader's compacted log; SEND_SNAP re-sends the same snapshot, whose success resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (replication.go:360-376, 588-599) — repeating full snapshot transfers plus FSM restores with the peer's match index pinned at the snapshot index. Recorded as one Behavior (the asymmetry with restoreUserSnapshot), one Fact (the cycle with its three required conditions), and an 'explained' interpretation listing the refutations (snapshot preferred when the cached index is lower; leader able to walk below the divergence; other terminating conditions) and the competition (correct FSM state, so the harm is repeated nonprogress/work rather than divergence). Two earlier suspicions were discarded after checking: installSnapshot's missing setLastLog is harmless in the ordinary index-behind case, and the commitment median index is correct for even voter counts.
